comment: Staging pass-through of append-only bronze (see README's "Why bronze never overwrites for Elexon"): the same settlement_date+settlement_period appears once per past landing by design, so there is no single-row-per-key grain to test at this layer. Resolution to one row happens in silver.
Same reasoning as stg_elexon_system_prices: append-only bronze pass-through, resolved to one row per key in silver, not here.

Bronze can contain duplicate landings per half hour by design (the extractor runs every 30 minutes and can re-fetch periods it has already seen); silver_regional_intensity is where one row per valid_from+region_id gets picked.

An audit log of every price change ever observed for a settlement_date+settlement_period, not a one-row-per-key table -- a key genuinely can have more than one logged revision, so there is no combination of columns that is meant to be unique here.
Same reasoning as silver__price_revisions: an audit log, not a one-row-per-key table.
A static 50-row dimension generated from generate_series(1, 50), not built from a ref() or source() -- correctly has zero parents by design, not a missing dependency.

All three marts read from the central settlement-period fact directly, by design, in a project this size -- see the gold-layer README section. Revisit if the mart count grows well past three and this starts looking like a real hub-and-spoke problem rather than three dashboard-shaped views of one fact.

mart_daily_summary joins dim_date directly (as the date spine every day left-joins onto, so days with no data still appear) and dim_fuel_type directly (to categorise renewable/fossil/interconnector for the SUM(CASE...) aggregations), in addition to reaching both transitively through fct_generation. Intentional: the mart needs the raw dimension attributes for its own aggregation logic, not just whatever fct_generation already carries.
